correctness.rationale: Every distinct new one-type is an insertion-gap pair. Discrepancy two constrains the gaps to exactly \(3(n-1)\) candidate positions. Full saturation is equivalent to one outward crossing per initial cut and displacement at most two. The former forces a single spanning permutation cycle and, for \(n\ge4\), no fixed points; the latter makes that cycle Hamiltonian in the square of a path. The square has a unique undirected Hamilton cycle by an explicit edge-expansion induction, and its two orientations attain the bound. Direct small cases \(n=2,3\) complete the classification. The standard-library verifier checked 409112 permutations and independent direct definitions for small sizes; finite checks are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The all-size discrepancy-two insertion-type bound and rigid equality classification were compared against the foundational homogeneous-permutations construction, reduct classification, oligomorphic enumeration and current relevant mathematical-record searches. Cameron (2002) has the identical \(n=4\) equality patterns in a different adjacency theorem; we explicitly credit that endpoint and claim originality only for the general sharp type-count theorem and \(n\ge5\) rigidity. An equivalent formulation in older literature remains possible.

value.rationale: An intrinsically logical, discrete one-point-type filtration has a sharp maximal second-disagreement layer and a complete rigidity classification at every base size. The extremizers collapse to two inverse zigzag permutations for every n>=4, structurally different from the large disjoint-swap maximizing family at discrepancy one. The cut-to-Hamilton-cycle mechanism and unique Hamilton cycle induction explain and generalize the previously observed four-point pair; this is a motivated exact structural boundary, not a mere numerical increment.
